newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC NAME OLD ADVERSARY AS HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC NAME OLD ADVERSARY AS HEAD COACH.

text.p: Celtic turned to an old adversary in a bid to regain their status as a European power by naming former Feyenoord trainer Wim Jansen as head coach on Thursday.
The 53-year-old Dutchman, who has signed a three-year contract with the Scottish club, was responsible as a Feyenoord player in 1970 for defeating Celtic in the European Cup final.

Now he has been given the task of toppling Glasgow arch-rivals Rangers, who have won nine domestic titles in succesion, as well as revitalising Celtic's fortunes on the continent. They won the European Cup 30 years ago.
Jansen said: "Celtic have always had a special place in my memories because they were involved in the greatest day of my life in 1970 and I want to bring them back to the highest level.
"I am delighted to be joining such a famous club and it's a big challenge that I welcome."

More than 2,000 fans gathered outside Celtic Park when word leaked out of a news conference to announe the successor to Tommy Burns, who was sacked as manager 10 weeks ago after twice finishing runners-up to Rangers.

Jansen, who won 65 caps for the Netherlands and played in the 1974 World Cup final, said: "Since leaving Japan six months ago, I have had several offers in Holland but I wanted to wait for a big club, and I knew that Celtic were that club for me."

He agreed his new job in Glasgow was similar to the situation he faced in the Netherlands trying to topple Ajax, but added: "At Feyenoord I didn't have any money. It was a difficult situation but I have learned from that."
